annotationRationale: Uniform interval-length probabilities give the winning probability in each range of Carol's choice. Independence and disjoint-event addition produce the middle quadratic, whose vertex must be compared with the best outside values.
sourceMethod: Followed the official three-case probability calculation and maximized the middle quadratic using its vertex, then compared the resulting probability with the two outside cases.

review.mathCheck: The three cases give winning probabilities \(c\), \(-12c^2+13c-3\), and \(1-c\), with ties and boundary events having probability zero. The middle quadratic equals \(25/48-12(c-13/24)^2\), so its interior maximum is \(25/48\), exceeding the outside maxima 1/2 and 1/3. Choice B is correct.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA solution 24, page 15. It follows the same three cases and vertex comparison, explicitly explaining uniform interval ratios, independence, and disjoint-event addition.
review.annotationCheck: Uniform geometric probability and constrained quadratic maximization are appropriately assessed. Independence and probability addition support the model. All ranges, endpoints, and the comparison establishing a global maximum are covered.
